Surah Ha-Mim as-Sajdah (Fussilat)

[Meccan; its verses are 53 or 54; it was revealed after Ghafir]

﴿Ha-Mim.﴾ God knows best what He intends by it.
﴿A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ — "A revelation" is the subject (mubtada'), the predicate of which is implied.

Translation:

﴿A Book﴾, its predicate being ﴿whose verses have been detailed﴾, explained through the rulings, the narratives and the admonitions; ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to "a Book" by its description; ﴿for a people﴾, the phrase being connected to "have been detailed"; ﴿who know﴾, meaning who understand that, and they are the Arabs.

﴿بشيرا﴾ (bashīran, "a bringer of good news") is a ṣifah (qualifier) of ﴿قرآنا﴾ (qur'ānan, "a Qur'an"), ﴿ونذيرا﴾ (wa-nadhīran, "and a warner"). ﴿فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون﴾ "Yet most of them turned away, so they do not hear," meaning hearing of acceptance (samā' qabūl).

"And they said" (to the Prophet), "Our hearts are in coverings (akinna; coverings) from what you call us to, and in our ears is a deafness (waqr; heaviness), and between us and you is a barrier (hijab; disagreement in religion). So act" (on your religion), "for indeed we are acting" (on our religion).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 6:

﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is but one God. So take the straight path to Him"﴾ by faith and obedience, ﴿and seek His forgiveness.﴾ And woe ﴿(wayl)﴾ is a word of punishment.

The Jalalayn commentary on 41:7 is a single fragment here: "﴿The ones who do not give zakat, and they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.﴾" — translated below.

﴿Those who do not give zakat, and they, concerning the Hereafter, they are [disbelievers]﴾ — "هم" is an emphatic reinforcement (ta'kid).

Note on the source: the text as given ends at "تأكيد" and does not include the full sentence the Jalalayn normally has here, so the translation above renders only what appears in the passage.
﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is never cut off.﴾ *Maqtu'* (cut off)

Say, "Do you truly disbelieve in the One Who created the earth in ﴿two days﴾, the Sunday and the Monday, and set up ﴿rivals﴾ (shuraka', partners) to Him?" ﴿That is the Lord (rabb), i.e., the Owner (malik) of the ﴿worlds﴾."

Regarding the recitation of the interrogative ﴿أإنكم﴾: the second hamza is read with تحقيق الهمزة (tahqiq al-hamza, pronouncing the hamza fully) or with تسهيلها (tashil, softening it), and an alif is inserted between it and the first hamza, according to both readings of the second hamza.

The word ﴿العالمين﴾ is the plural of عالم ('alam, world), which refers to everything other than God. It is pluralized with the ya' and nun ending (ين) because its kinds differ, and this follows the principle of تغليب (taghlib, giving precedence to rational beings), since the rational are given priority in grammatical gender.

Wa-ja'ala ("and He placed") is a new clause (mustaʼnaf), and it is not permissible to make it a conjunction with the relative clause of alladhi, because of the intervening foreign element. ﴿And He placed in it firm mountains﴾ — mountains that are fixed — ﴿from above it, and blessed in it﴾ — with abundance of waters, crops and livestock — ﴿and apportioned in it its sustenance﴾ — divided it — ﴿for the people and the animals﴾ — ﴿in﴾ the completion of ﴿four days﴾, meaning the placing and what was mentioned with it, on Tuesday and Wednesday. ﴿Equal﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning the four days were equal, neither more nor less. ﴿For those who ask﴾ — about the creation of the earth and what is in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 11:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾ He intended (qasd) toward (ila) the heaven, and it was a rising vapour (bukhar murtafi'). ﴿So He said to it and to the earth: Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly.﴾ Come to what I desire from you both. ﴿Willingly or unwillingly﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning: obedient or compelled. ﴿They both said: We come willingly.﴾ With those among us [in us]. ﴿Willingly﴾ here is in the masculine plural form, which is the dominance (taghlib) of the masculine rational gender; or they (the two) were treated as those who are addressed in this manner (nazzalatā li-khitābihimā manzilatahu).

Then He decreed them as seven heavens in two days. The pronoun refers back to "the heaven," because it carries the sense of a plural, to which it is tending. That is, He made them (﴿سبع سماوات في يومين﴾) seven heavens in two days: Thursday and Friday. He finished them in the last hour of Friday, and in it Adam was created. For this reason He did not say here "equal" (sawa'), and what is here agrees with the verses on the creation of the heavens and the earth in six days. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its affair﴾, that is, the obedience and worship which He commanded those in it to perform. ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, that is, with stars, ﴿and as a guard﴾, accusative by a suppressed verb, meaning: We guarded it from the stealing of hearing by the devils, by means of shooting stars. ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty﴾ in His kingdom, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ concerning His creation.

﴿Then if they turn away﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah turn away from faith after this clarification, ﴿say, "I have warned you﴾ I have frightened you ﴿of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾ a punishment that will destroy you, like that which destroyed them.

﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾, i.e., coming at them and departing from them, so they disbelieved, as will be mentioned, and the destruction was in their time only. ﴿That﴾, i.e., that ﴿do not worship except Allah,﴾ they said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down﴾ upon us ﴿angels. Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾ according to your claim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 15:

﴿As for ʿĀd, they were arrogant in the land without right, and said﴾ when they were warned of the punishment, ﴿"Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾ meaning, no one. One of them would uproot a great rock from the mountain and place it wherever he wished. ﴿Did they not see﴾ i.e., did they not know ﴿that God, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they were rejecting Our signs﴾ the miracles.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 16:

﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾ cold, intensely loud, without rain, ﴿in days of misfortune﴾ (with the ḥāʾ vocalized with a kasra or with a sukūn), ill-omened for them, ﴿that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace﴾ the humiliation, ﴿in the life of this world; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾ more severe, ﴿and they will not be helped﴾ by having it withheld from them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 17:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾ We made clear to them the way of guidance, ﴿but they preferred blindness﴾ they chose disbelief ﴿over guidance. So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾ the humiliating one.
﴿And We saved﴾ from it ﴿those who believed and were God-fearing﴾ Allah

ۚ"And mention" ﴿the Day when﴾ "the enemies of Allah are gathered" (with ya' and with nun opened, damma on the shin and fatha on the hamza) ﴿to the Fire, and they will be driven in ranks﴾ meaning, they will be driven.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 20:

﴿Until, when﴾ [i.e., ﴿ما﴾ is] superfluous (zā'idah)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 21:

﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who made everything speak."﴾ That is, He willed its speech. ﴿And it is He who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ It is said: this is part of the speech of the skins; and it is said: this is part of the speech of Allah, Exalted, like what follows it. Its placement is close to what precedes it, in that the One who is able to originate your creation and return you alive after death is able to make your skins and your limbs speak.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 22:

﴿You did not used to conceal yourselves﴾ from committing your abominations, ﴿lest your hearing, nor your eyes, nor your skins should testify against you﴾, because you did not have certainty in the resurrection. ﴿Rather, you thought﴾ when you concealed yourselves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 23:

﴿And that﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), ﴿your opinion﴾ is an apposition (badal) from it, ﴿which you held about your Lord﴾ is a qualifier (na't), and the predicate (khabar) is ﴿has destroyed you﴾, meaning: has ruined you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 24:

﴿Then if they endure patiently﴾ the punishment, ﴿the Fire is their abode﴾, their dwelling place, ﴿for them. And if they ask to be forgiven﴾, seeking al-'utba (ʿutbā), that is, contentment, ﴿they will not be among those who are granted it﴾, those who are pleased.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 25:

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾ (qarana'), i.e., We caused them to be (sabbabna) companions for them, ﴿from the devils﴾, ﴿who made attractive to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of the world and the pursuit of desires, ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, by their saying: there is no resurrection and no reckoning. ﴿And the word became due against them﴾ of punishment, and it is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell"﴾ (the verse), ﴿among﴾ the company of ﴿nations that had passed away﴾, i.e., perished.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a concise classical commentary) on surah 41, verse 26:

﴿And those who disbelieve said﴾ when the Prophet (ﷺ) was reciting, ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it﴾: bring in commotion (al-laghat) and the like, and shout during the time of its recitation, ﴿so that you may overcome﴾, so that he falls silent from the recitation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 27:

﴿So We will surely make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ That is, the most evil recompense of their deeds.

﴿That﴾ the severe punishment and the worst recompense, ﴿is the recompense of the enemies of Allah﴾, with the second hamza in أَعْدَاءُ realized in full (taḥqīq) and also replaced with a waw (ibdāl). ﴿The Fire﴾ is an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to the recompense mentioned as the subject of the statement. ﴿For them therein is the abode of eternity﴾, meaning a lasting dwelling from which there is no removal. ﴿Recompense﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar) governed by its implied verb. ﴿For what they used to deny of Our signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

"And those who disbelieved will say [in the Fire], 'Our Lord, show us those who led us astray from among the jinn and mankind'—i.e., Iblis and Qabil, who initiated disbelief and killing—'that we may put them beneath our feet [in the Fire] so that they will be among the lowest.'" i.e., more severe in punishment than us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 30:

﴿Indeed, those who said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast﴾ upon the Tawhid (Oneness of God) and other things that were obligatory upon them, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear﴾ death and what comes after it, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over what you have left behind of family and children, for We will be their successors concerning them."

﴿We are your allies in the worldly life and in the Hereafter.﴾ i.e., We guard you in it. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ i.e., We will be with you in it, until you enter Paradise. ﴿And therein you shall have whatever your souls desire, and therein you shall have whatever you ask for.﴾ ﴿Tadda'un﴾ means you request.

﴿نزلا﴾ (*nuzulan*): a provision, prepared, accusative (*manṣūb*, the grammatical case of the object) governed by an implied verb *ja'ala* (made/provided). ﴿From the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, i.e., Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 33:

﴿Who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah﴾ meaning: no one is better in speech ﴿than one who invites to Allah﴾ to monotheism (tawhid).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 41, verse 34:

﴿Good and evil are not equal.﴾ In their particulars, because one of them is above the other. ﴿Repel [evil]﴾ with that which is ﴿better﴾, i.e., with the quality that is best, such as repelling anger with patience, ignorance with forbearance, and offense with pardon. ﴿Then he between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as if he were a close friend.﴾ That is, your enemy will become like a close friend in affection if you do that. Al-ladhi (the one who) is the subject (mubtada'), kaannahu (as if he) is the predicate (khabar), and idha (then) is an adverb indicating the sense of comparison.

ﷻ"And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great good fortune" (﴿وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم﴾ is the full verse; the passage here quotes its parts).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: ﴿وما يلقاها﴾, i.e., none is granted the quality that is better (أي يؤتي الخصلة التي هي أحسن), ﴿إلا الذين صبروا﴾ except those who endure patiently, ﴿وما يلقها إلا ذو حظ﴾ and none is granted it except one possessing a share, meaning reward (ثواب).

["And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you" — translation follows]

**Translation:**

﴿And if﴾ — here the nūn of the conditional particle "in" (إن) is assimilated into the superfluous "mā" (ما). ﴿an evil suggestion from Satan prompts you﴾ — i.e., some diverting influence turns you away from the good trait and from other goodness. ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾ — this is the answer to the condition; the answer to the command is omitted, i.e., He will repel it from you. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of speech, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 37:

﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ That is, the four signs (al-ayat al-arba').

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 38:

﴿Then if they are arrogant﴾ [i.e., against prostrating to Allah alone], ﴿those who are with your Lord﴾ [i.e., the angels] ﴿glorify Him﴾ [i.e., pray] ﴿by night and day, and they never tire﴾ [i.e., they do not grow weary].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 39:

﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells.﴾ Barren (يابسة), with no vegetation in it. ﴿When We send down water upon it, it stirs﴾ (تحركت) moves, ﴿and swells﴾ (وربت) expands and rises.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses﴾ — from alhada and lahada — ﴿in Our verses﴾ — the Qur'an — by denying them, ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾, so We will recompense them. ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do as you wish; indeed He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ — a threat to them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 41, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿when it came to them﴾ — We will requite them. ﴿And indeed, it is a Book of might﴾ — invulnerable.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 42:

﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy.﴾ That is: there is no scripture before it that refutes it, nor one after it.

﴿A revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ That is: Allah, who is praiseworthy in His command.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 43:

﴿What is said to you﴾ of denial ﴿is not but﴾ the like of ﴿what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness﴾ for the believers ﴿and Possessor of painful punishment﴾ for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 44:

﴿And if We had made it﴾ i.e., the Reminder, ﴿a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not explained in detail?"﴾ i.e., "Why are its verses not made clear?" ﴿so that we may understand them﴾. ﴿What! [Is it] a non-Arabic [Qur'an] and [the Prophet] an Arab?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial on their part, with the second hamzah pronounced as is, or changed into an alif, with or without prolongation. ﴿Say: "It is, for those who believe, a guidance﴾ from misguidance ﴿and a healing﴾ from ignorance. ﴿As for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears﴾ a heaviness, so they do not hear it, ﴿and it is blindness for them﴾ so they do not understand it. ﴿They are those who are called from a far place﴾ i.e., they are like one being called from a far place, who neither hears nor understands what he is being called to."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 45:

﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾ — the Torah — ﴿but it was disputed over﴾ — with some confirming it and some denying it, just as with the Qur'an — ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ — namely, the deferral of the reckoning and the recompense of creatures until the Day of Resurrection — ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ — in this world, concerning what they disputed — ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾ — i.e., the deniers of it — ﴿doubt that causes suspicion﴾ — that brings about uneasiness.

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self﴾ [i.e., whoever] does [a good deed], ﴿and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, i.e., the harm of his evil deed falls upon himself. ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, i.e., not one who does injustice, because of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] even by the weight of an atom﴾.

To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour (﴿إليه يرد علم الساعة﴾), i.e., when it will occur; none other than Him knows it. ﴿And no fruit comes out of its sheaths﴾ (﴿وما تخرج من ثمرات﴾), and in another reading "fruits" (ثمرات) is read in the plural form, ﴿from their husks﴾ (﴿من أكمامها﴾), i.e., their containers (أوعيتها), the plural of kumm (كم) with a kasra on the kaf, ﴿except with His knowledge﴾ (﴿إلا بعلمه﴾). ﴿Nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge﴾ (﴿وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه﴾). ﴿And on the day He will call to them: "Where are My partners?"﴾ (﴿ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي﴾), they will say: ﴿"We have informed You"﴾ (﴿قالوا آذناك﴾), i.e., We have made You know now (أعلمناك الآن), ﴿"that none of us is a witness"﴾ (﴿ما منا من شهيد﴾), i.e., a witness that You have a partner.

﴿And there was lost to them﴾ vanished (ghāba) ﴿what they used to call upon﴾, i.e., worship, ﴿before﴾, i.e., in the world, of the idols, ﴿and they thought﴾, i.e., were certain, ﴿that they had no escape﴾, i.e., no flight or refuge from the punishment. The negation (ما) in both places is suspended from operating (ta'līq) on the verb, and the negative clause took the place of the two objects (سدت مسد المفعولين).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 49:

﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾, i.e., he never ceases to ask his Lord for wealth, health and other things. ﴿But if evil touches him﴾, poverty and hardship, ﴿then he is despairing, hopeless﴾ of the mercy of God. This and what follows refers to the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 50:

﴿And if﴾ the lam is a lam of oath. ﴿We let him taste﴾ We give him ﴿mercy﴾ wealth and health ﴿from Us after adversity﴾ hardship and affliction ﴿has touched him, he will surely say: "This is mine"﴾ i.e., by my own effort. ﴿And I do not think the Hour will establish itself. And if﴾ the lam is a lam of oath ﴿I am returned to my Lord, indeed I shall have with Him the best [reward]﴾ i.e., Paradise. ﴿Then We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste of a severe punishment﴾ harsh, and the lam in the verb is a lam of oath.

﴿And when We bestow favour upon man﴾ the species (al-jins) ﴿he turns away﴾ from thankfulness ﴿and withdraws to his side﴾ he bends his side aside, swaggering (mutabakhtiran). In another recitation (qira'a, a canonical variant reading), the hamza is placed before the nun, reading ﴿أَنْأَى﴾. ﴿But when evil touches him, then he is one of long supplication﴾ abundant, i.e. much (kathir).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 41, verse 52:

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ That is, the Qur'an, ﴿from Allah﴾, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said. ﴿Then you disbelieve in it﴾; ﴿who is more astray﴾, that is, no one is, ﴿than one who is in opposition﴾, meaning dissension, ﴿far﴾ from the truth. Here the phrase "who is" is placed in the position of "you," to clarify their state.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 53:

﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ the regions of the heavens and the earth, [shown] in the luminous bodies, the plants and the trees, ﴿and within themselves﴾ [shown] in the subtle craftsmanship and the wondrous wisdom, ﴿until it becomes clear to them that it﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is the truth﴾ sent down from God, [concerning] the resurrection, the reckoning and the punishment, so that they will be punished for their disbelief in it and in the one who brought it. ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord﴾ the subject of "yakfi" (suffice), ﴿that He is over all things a witness?﴾ a substitute for it, i.e., is it not sufficient for them as regards your truthfulness that your Lord is not absent from Him in anything whatsoever?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 41, verse 54:

﴿Verily, they are in doubt﴾ (i.e., in suspicion) ﴿about the meeting with their Lord﴾ because they deny the Resurrection. ﴿Verily, He﴾ (exalted is He) ﴿encompasses all things﴾ in knowledge and power, so He will recompense them for their disbelief.
